results.fact: Whether a wilderness permit is needed
results.evidence: Still present: permit and access.permit say a free self-issue wilderness permit at the trailhead, while the trailhead waypoint directions, itinerary.cal and access.overnight_permit say no permit is needed. The Forest Service boundary layer confirms the summit is inside the Wild Sky Wilderness, but the Wild Sky page mentions only recreation passes and wilderness regulations, the forest-wide wilderness page says only that day visitors 'may need' a free self-issue permit without naming which areas, and a peak-area page describes a free trailhead registration. No two sources state whether Wild Sky uses a self-issue permit. No patch.

results.fact: Where the approach starts: North Fork Skykomish Trailhead (end of FR-63) vs an unmarked river-crossing pullout near Galena (~Mile 10, ~1,150 ft)
results.evidence: approach and approach_logistics start at the North Fork Skykomish Trailhead at the end of FR-63 (trailhead pin 47.927, -121.277, about 12 km from the summit) and access.fees/parking_pass describe that trailhead's pass, while the trailhead waypoint and itinerary.cal park at an unmarked turnaround by the river crossing near Galena at about 1,150 ft, with a hogsback-ridge line of waypoints that does not match the approach text's route up the north side. These are two different starting points. Not researched to a settled answer in this pass (and both approach roads are currently closed per access.closures); left for research.

results.fact: Grade disagreement: Class 4 / 5.4 vs. the route's own 5.6 crux
results.evidence: Still present: grade 'Class 4', rock_grade '5.4', beta and pitch_detail '5.6'. New descriptions agree only loosely: the peak's route page calls the Itswoot Ridge / Spire Col route Class 4 with a friction slab for the final 50 ft and an optional low-5th-class 15 ft summit block; a trip report and its partner rated the crux low 5th class; another report expected class 4-5. No two sources give the same YDS number (5.4 or 5.6), so no grade is adopted.

results.fact: Itswoot Ridge camp elevation: waypoint 6,600 ft vs approach ~6,400 ft vs bivy 5,880 ft
results.correct_value: 6,400 ft for the Itswoot Ridge camp beside the stream draining the Spire Point basin
results.evidence: The waypoint describes the specific camp on the ridge beside the stream running down from Spire Point. The peak's route page puts that camp at 6,400 ft (room for 3-4 tents, stream from the Spire Point area beside the ridge), and a 2019 trip report gives Itswoot Ridge camps at 6,400 ft (or a higher one at 6,900 ft); the row's own approach text also says ~6,400 ft. waypoints[4].elev 6,600 is corrected to 6,400. bivy[0] (5,880) explicitly describes the lower, wetter end of the ridge and quotes the 5,900-6,400 ft range, so it is a different bench and is left.

patches.fact: Itswoot Ridge camp elevation: waypoint 6,600 ft vs approach ~6,400 ft vs bivy 5,880 ft

results.evidence: Still present. The 5,200 ft / 22 mi round-trip figure traces to a single route listing for the Southwest Spur (8.7 mi to Fish Creek Pass); a regional hiking page gives only 7.5 mi and 3,500 ft to Star Lake; a combined Courtney + Star Peak outing gives 18 mi and 6,400 ft, which includes a second summit. No second independent source states the Star Peak-only cumulative gain. No patch.

results.fact: Where the climbers' path leaves the maintained trail (Park Creek Pass traverse vs the ~4,100 ft washout on the Park Creek trail)
results.correct_value: Low start from the Park Creek valley (climbers' trail up the ridge into the southwest basin)
results.evidence: The evidence now leans more clearly to the low start: the peak's route page describes a climbers' trail up the ridge (ash, burn, deadfall) that fades into diagonal heather and game-trail travel into the endless southwest basin, with about 5,100 ft of gain from Park Creek Camp (2,280 ft) to the summit, and a trip report descended from the basin to the Park Creek trail. No source describes a high traverse west from Park Creek Pass. Correcting the row means rewriting the approach, several waypoint directions and approach_variants into one consistent narrative, which is a rebuild rather than a minimal patch; left for that pass with the direction established.

results.evidence: Still present. results.fact: Whether a wilderness permit is needed
results.evidence: Still present. The Forest Service boundary layer confirms the summit is inside the Wild Sky Wilderness (the Barclay Lake trailhead is outside it), so naming Wild Sky is right; the open question is only whether Wild Sky uses a free self-issue permit. The Wild Sky page mentions only recreation passes and regulations, the forest-wide page says day visitors 'may need' a self-issue permit without naming areas, and one peak-area page mentions a free trailhead registration. Not settled by two sources. No patch.

results.fact: Thunder Basin high-camp elevation: 6,400 ft (waypoint) vs. ~5,180 ft (approach text and itinerary schedule)
results.evidence: Still present. Both heights are used as camps (upper basin ~5,180 ft in one account; bivy platforms at 6,400 ft above the tarns in another), and the ground at the waypoint's pin reads ~5,029 ft, matching neither. No new source identifies which is the standard high camp. No patch.
